assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED made a controllable, strongly coupled light-matter regime available on a chip: a superconducting artificial atom coupled to a single microwave resonator mode, with dispersive readout, vacuum Rabi splitting and photon-number-resolved control. It opened a genuinely new regime and became the common architecture of superconducting quantum processors and of microwave quantum optics generally. I know this area closely and judge the discovery both clean and foundational.
assessment.attribution: The 2004 proposal (Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin, Schoelkopf) and the first strong-coupling experiment (Wallraff et al., Schoelkopf group) support a Schoelkopf, Wallraff and Girvin configuration. Blais is a decisive theory contributor and the choice of three leaves him out, which is a real attribution tension. Credit for the underlying circuits (Devoret, Martinis, Clarke) was already recognized in 2025.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by dozens of laboratories for twenty years, with an interpretation that is stable and heavily built upon. Timing is a question: the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits is close in subject, so the committee should ask whether cQED is a distinct discovery or an extension of that recognition.
uncertainties: Whether a second prize in superconducting circuits so soon after 2025 is appropriate.
Blais versus Girvin as the theory laureate; I am relying on recollection of the 2004 papers rather than verifying them.
My own field and directorship of a quantum-technology programme create a potential conflict of interest in discussion; I note it candidly.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock (Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and demonstration; Ye's push to 10^-18 and below with strontium) turned many-atom interrogation into the most accurate measurement devices ever built, with consequences for redefinition of the second, relativistic geodesy and tests of fundamental constants. The physics is clean, quantitative and controlled to every physical detail.
assessment.attribution: Katori is the originator of the magic-wavelength lattice idea; Ye is the leading figure in realising ultra-high-accuracy and high-coherence lattice clocks. A two-person prize is natural. Ye also appears in the thorium-229 candidate; that overlap does not matter here. Other contributors (Takamoto, Ludlow, Lemonde, Pfeiffer) exist, but I see no serious dispute over the principal credit.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed across many independent groups (JILA, RIKEN, NIST, SYRTE, PTB, NPL and others), mature and still improving. Frequency-comb metrology was recognised in 2005, so this builds on rather than repeats an earlier prize. The redefinition of the SI second has not yet happened, which does not affect scientific merit.
uncertainties: The 2005 comb prize may be seen as having already covered part of the metrological narrative.
Precise priority between Katori's and Ye's contributions, and the role of the lattice-clock proposal by Katori versus related earlier ideas, is from memory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cirac and Zoller's 1995 proposal for quantum gates with trapped ions and the experimental demonstrations that followed established the first credible and still leading platform for quantum logic with very high fidelity; related theory of quantum simulation with cold atoms and ions broadened the impact. Intellectually it is a clean example of foundational theory turned into an experimental platform.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller are clearly decisive as the theory originators. On the experimental side Blatt is a strong candidate, but Wineland (already a 2012 laureate) and Monroe, Wineland, Leibfried and others also made decisive contributions to the first gates, so the experimental credit is a real question and the three-name list is not obviously complete.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally very mature, with independent confirmation across many ion-trap groups and a stable interpretation. The 2012 prize to Wineland and Haroche for measuring and manipulating single quantum systems partly overlaps, so the committee must articulate what is new.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize and with Wineland's earlier credit.
Whether the combined theory-plus-ions-plus-atoms description is a single discovery or compounds different ones that need separate recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BB84 and E91 established that quantum mechanics can secure communication, linking entanglement and no-cloning to a concrete protocol. The ideas have a fundamental character (information-theoretic security from physical law) and are experimentally realised over fibre and satellite links. The Nobel-worthiness is high as a conceptual contribution, though much of the story is information-theoretic rather than a measured new physical phenomenon.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard for BB84 are clear. Ekert for entanglement-based E91 is well supported, and Bell-test related ground was covered in 2022. Mayers, Lo and others on security proofs, and Wiesner on conjugate coding, complicate credit but are not in the supplied credit list.
assessment.maturity: Protocols are long confirmed; implementations are commercial and sound. Practical security of real devices (side channels) is a separate issue and not decisive. Timeliness is fine, though the 2022 entanglement prize reduces novelty.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as physics rather than computer science or cryptography.
Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea is not available among the credited names, so the fairest configuration is unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices give controllable realisations of Hubbard-type models, with the superfluid to Mott insulator transition, fermionic Hubbard physics and single-site-resolved microscopy. They make a many-body quantum regime directly visible and tunable, which is the kind of basic phenomenon I value, and they are an important enabling platform for analogue quantum simulation.
assessment.attribution: Bloch, Greiner and Esslinger are the leading experimentalists; Zoller's theory (also in B009) and Jaksch's 1998 proposal are decisive for the theory origin, so the proposal that experiments realise has an unresolved credit question. The supplied list with four names does not fit a three-person prize, and the 2001 BEC prize and 2018 and 2012 prizes overlap in the community.
assessment.maturity: Strong, independent confirmation by many groups, though quantum simulation is still moving towards demonstrating advantage over classical methods; the headline problems (for example the doped Hubbard model phase diagram) are not settled.
uncertainties: Which of the two or three experimentalists is the most decisive.
Theory credit to Zoller, which would overlap with the B009 configuration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Squeezed light for quantum-limited measurement links a basic quantum-optics idea (Caves 1981) to an important practical result: squeezed states in gravitational-wave interferometers. This fits the 2017 LIGO prize and gives a clear example of foundational physics enabling an instrument.
assessment.attribution: Caves for the theoretical proposal for interferometers is clear. Kimble (first observation of squeezing in Slusher's era with colleagues) and Schnabel (GEO600 and LIGO implementations) are possible, but the early experimental squeezing credit to Slusher, Yurke and Walls and the LIGO implementation credit (Mavalvala, McKenzie, Vahlbruch) make attribution untidy.
assessment.maturity: Squeezing in operating observatories is established and independently reproduced. Maturity is high; the narrative is fragmented across many contributors.
uncertainties: Attribution is genuinely contested, and some decisive experimental contributors are not in the three names I can propose.
Whether the committee would view the LIGO application as already rewarded in 2017.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cavity optomechanics brought mechanical motion into the quantum regime: ground-state cooling, quantum-limited measurement, squeezing and entanglement of mechanical oscillators. Cleland's 2010 demonstration of a mechanical resonator in its ground state coupled to a superconducting qubit is a particularly clean quantum demonstration; I know the related circuit-phonon work.
assessment.attribution: Aspelmeyer and Kippenberg are the leading optomechanics figures; Cleland is the leading figure for quantum acoustics with superconducting circuits. Others (Painter, Lehnert, Schwab, Harris, Teufel) made decisive demonstrations, so credit is spread widely and any three-person set looks arbitrary.
assessment.maturity: The field is maturing, with multiple independent demonstrations, but the lasting scientific consequence (quantum sensing, transduction, tests of macroscopic quantum mechanics) is still developing, so the prize may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Possible prematurity relative to the field's eventual impact.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum error-correcting codes and fault-tolerant constructions show in principle that large quantum computations are possible despite noise, and topological codes give a physical route to protection. As a theorist working on gate fidelity I regard this as central to the field, and its relevance to a future quantum computer is clear, but I also stress that this is the idea that has yet to be fully demonstrated at scale.
assessment.attribution: Shor (first code and fault tolerance) and Steane (CSS-type codes) are decisive, and Kitaev for the toric code and anyons. Calderbank, Gottesman, Knill, Laflamme, Aharonov, Ben-Or, Preskill and Zurek are also decisive, so the list of three is a thin subset of a crowded history.
assessment.maturity: Experimental demonstrations are recent and encouraging (below-threshold surface-code memories), but a scalable fault-tolerant machine is not yet there. Recognition now would be early relative to the stated applications, although the theory itself is stable.
uncertainties: Credit is widely distributed, and the three-person selection is difficult to defend.
Whether the prize should wait for demonstrated fault tolerance.
Overlap with Kitaev's role in B027 topological superconductivity.
